en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Dukadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (6) 24.4.
Hetuduka, Āsavagocchaka (The Group on Taints within the Dyads on Causes)
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor an outflow, a state that is a root and an outflow arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor an outflow, a state that is neither a root nor an outflow arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor an outflow, states that are both roots and outflows and states that are neither roots nor outflows arise by way of root-condition. ... [Three.]
Dependent on a state that is neither a cause nor an outflow (*na-hetu no-āsava*), a state that is a cause and an outflow arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … one.

Dependent on states that are neither causes nor outflows, and [dependent on] states that are neither causes nor outflows, a state that is a cause and an outflow arises by way of root-condition … one. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are five … pe … under non-disappearance there are five.
Dependent on a state that is neither a cause nor an outflow, a state that is neither a cause nor an outflow arises by way of root-condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor-outflow, a state that is neither-root but not-outflow arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor-outflow, a state that is root but not-outflow arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor-outflow, states that are both root but not-outflow and neither-root nor-outflow arise by way of root-condition. … three.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor an outflow and has neither a root nor an outflow, a state that is neither a root nor an outflow arises by way of root condition... [one] (abridged). Under root condition there are five... up to ... under non-disappearance there are five.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor an outflow, a state that is neither a root but is an outflow arises by way of root condition. (Abridged). Under root condition there are three; under predominance there are three... up to ... under non-disappearance there are three.

Conditioned by a state that is neither a root nor associated with taints (*na-hetu na-āsava*), a state that is a root and free from taints arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance there are three.

In dependence on a state that is neither a root nor associated with taints, a state that is a root and associated with taints arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance there are three.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor dissociated from the taints (*āsava*), a state that is a root and dissociated from the taints arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Nine in the case of the root; three in the case of the object; ... [and so on] ... nine in the case of non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root and neither with-taints (*āsava*) nor without-taints, a state that is a root and both with-taints and subject to taints (*sāsava*) arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Five in the case of the root; ... [and so on] ... five in the case of non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor an outflow (*na-hetu na-āsava*) and is also not associated with an outflow (*na-āsava-vippayutta*), there arises a state that is a root, is an outflow, and is also not associated with an outflow, by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under the root [condition], there are five... [etc. ...under the non-disappearance [condition], there are five.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor an outflow and is also dissociated from an outflow (*na-āsava-vippayutta*), there arises a state that is a root, is an outflow, and is also associated with an outflow (*āsava-sampayutta*), by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root [condition], there are three... [etc. ...under the non-disappearance [condition], there are three.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause (*na-hetu*), dissociated from the taints (*āsavavippayutta*), and itself not a taint (*na-āsava*), there arises a state that is a root-cause, associated with the taints, and itself not a taint, by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under the root-condition, there are three; ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*), there are three.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause, dissociated from the taints, and itself not a taint, there arises a state that is a root-cause, dissociated from the taints, and itself a taint (*sāsava*), by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root-condition, there are three; under the predominance condition (*adhipati*), there are three; ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition, there are three.

Conditioned by a state that is not a root, dissociated from the taints, and not itself a taint, there arises a state that is a root, dissociated from the taints, and not itself a taint, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance there are three.
